name: filter-menu
purpose: The list filter of a console list: a Filter button that carries the number of applied filters and opens a drill-in menu. The first level lists the fields, each with a summary of what is applied to it; picking a field slides to its values (check rows for a `multi` field, radio rows for a `single` one, an optional avatar per value, a search box and a no-match line), and a `date` field offers periods plus a custom range on a `Calendar`. Back returns to the fields, Clear removes the field's filter, and the panel's height follows each level. `FilterMenu.Chips` shows the applied fields as chips under the controls row: the field label in muted ink, an avatar stack, the first value and `+N`; activating a chip reopens the menu at that field, removing it clears the field. The value is a `Record<fieldId, values[]>` bound with `v-model`; the menu never filters anything itself. `Table.Filter` and `Table.AppliedFilters` render it with `kind="menu"` and map it onto the table's `filters` model. It differs from `property-filter` (one text field that builds `property operator value` tokens and combines them with and/or) and from the `table-filter` builder (a field + operator + value form): this menu offers only the values a field has, one click each, which is what most lists need.
useWhen: A resource list or table filtered by a few closed-set fields (status, owner, region, type) and a modification date.
A catalog or listing page (marketplace, templates, posts) that narrows by category, author or date, outside a table.
Filters people pick rather than type, where each field has a short list of values.
avoidWhen: Filters typed as text, with operators or and/or logic, or a query people keep as text → use `property-filter`. FilterMenu is for faceted picks from known values; PropertyFilter is for expression search.
A table that needs comparisons on numbers or free-text conditions → use `table-filter` with its builder.
Two to four fixed choices always on screen → use `toggle-group` or selectable `chip`s.
A single search over names → use `input`, or `table-search` inside a table.
related: table` — `Table.Filter` and `Table.AppliedFilters` with `kind="menu"` render this menu and its chips over the table's `filters` model.
property-filter` — the token-based filter field for typed queries.
popover` — the overlay the menu opens in.
calendar` — the range picker the custom date period uses.
bestPractices: Put the Filter button first in the controls row, before the search field, and `FilterMenu.Chips` on its own row below the controls.
Pass the same `fields` array and the same `v-model` to the menu and to its chips: chips reopen the menu that shares their `fields`.
Give people-like values an `avatar` (an image URL, or `''` for initials) so the chip shows who is filtered.
Keep each field to the values that exist in the data; a field with no values is noise.
Filter the data in the page (or on the server) from the model; read a date preset value (`24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `3m`) as a window ending now and a range value as its `start` and `end`.

props.name: fields
props.doc: Fields the menu lists, in order, each with its kind and values.

props.name: label
props.doc: Text of the trigger button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Filter`).

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token of the trigger button.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the trigger: the menu does not open.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound).
